LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. home.headline: Texans Have Two Offensive Injuries to Monitor After TNF Win
home.blurb: According to an update from the Texans during Thursday night's game, wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip) and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (stinger) would be deemed questionable for a return in the fourth quarter. We ultimately wound up seeing neither return to the action. But given that the Texans were so close to ending the game, it's unclear as to whether or not either player was dealing with a serious injury issue, or were simply being held out for precautionary reasons as the result of the game had already been decided. Rutledge was cleared to return on a short week against the Colts, but now after the same injury has surfaced once again, there might be a slim chance that Houston's first-round rookie is set to miss a little more time moving forward. As for Boutte, his hip injury seems to be a new issue to surface throughout Thursday night, which turned out to be a pretty successful night on his behalf. The Houston Texans put together a commanding win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night en route to a 26-3 victory that might just be the spark needed to help this team rattle off a few wins in a row through the second half of their season. However, in the midst of the Texans winning effort over the Colts, the team also saw their offense suffer a pair of injuries that will be worth keeping an eye on as they approach their next matchup. However, seeing both Boutte and Rutledge go down with an injury––each of whom has their respective key roles on the Texans' offense––is less than an ideal end to an overall successful night for Houston altogether. Kayshon Boutte, Keylan Rutledge Have Injuries to Keep Watch Of One of these injuries has been an issue the Texans have already seen surface earlier in the month, and that's the stinger that Rutledge suffered that makes for his second stinger in the past two weeks. The first stinger for Rutledge was bad enough that it led to him being sidelined for an entire week of the Texans' team practice , along with missing Week 10's game against the Cleveland Browns, forcing fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu into his first-ever start. Boutte converted on both of his targets against the Colts for two catches, 40 yards, and an aggressive touchdown reception in the second quarter for C.J. Stroud's second of three touchdown passes on the night––making for his second game on the season where he's seen over 40 yards in a single game. If Boutte is forced to miss any time, it'd mark yet another injury to the Texans’ wide receiver room following up on Jaylin Noel's injured reserve designation before Week 8 , along with the recent absence of Marvin Harrison Jr., which has led to him missing the last two games against the Browns and the Colts. The good news surrounding both of these injuries is that the Texans are able to get a mini-bye at their disposal before they're tasked with taking on their Week 13 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. away.headline: Miami Dolphins news roundup: Week 11 injury report includes Aaron Brewer update
away.blurb: The Miami Dolphins will be without punter Bradley Pinoin on Sunday as they face the Buffalo Bills. Pinion has a right groin injury and missed practice all week before being ruled out on Friday's injury report. Miami signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad this week and is expected to elevate him to the active roster by today's 4 p.m. Eastern deadline. Miami also ruled out wide receiver Jared Wayne for Sunday's game. He has a quadriceps injury. The Dolphins injury report included cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee) and safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin), both doubtful for the game. Cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee), center Aaron Brewer (concussion), and cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. (toe) are all questionable. Brewer, who missed last week's game with the head injury, fully participated in practice on Friday and, as long as he has no symptoms on Saturday, should be cleared to play. The Bills side of the reports includes cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) having been ruled out of the game while tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is doubtful. Safety Damar Hamlin (toe), defensive tackle T.J. Sanders (defensive tackle), and tight end Jackson Hawes (shoulder) are all questionable. You can check out more on the injury report news and other Dolphins news reports from around the web in this morning's edition of the Splash Zone: Dolphins' Hafley addresses who's in, who's out and who's in question for Sunday – Barry Jackson, Miami Herald The Dolphins have a good chance of getting back their starting center on Sunday at Buffalo, but they will likely be without one of their starting safeties. away.headline: Buffalo Bills vs. Miami Dolphins injury news: Ed Oliver questionable for Week 11
away.blurb: Oliver is now listed as questionable for Sunday’s home game, though the news is not all doom and gloom. Matt Parrino provided some context to Oliver’s injury , tweeting that “(p)er a league source, Ed Oliver notified Bills training staff this morning that he felt pain in his oblique. The staff checked it out and there’s optimism that he’ll play against the Dolphins.” Per NFL rules, Oliver’s ailment must be accounted for on the injury report even at this late stage, which is why he’s being listed as questionable. In the past, Oliver’s situation would have likely had him tabbed as “probable” for game day. The NFL has since done away with that injury designation, which has seen the questionable term pick up the slack in filing injuries throughout the league. Should Oliver be unable to go (or limited in some fashion) it would be a huge blow to Buffalo’s defense, which already has to account for injuries to starters in cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams. Both Bills defenders have been ruled out ahead of Week 11 . The injuries continue piling up for the Buffalo Bills ahead of their Week 11 home game against the Miami Dolphins. A surprise report originating from the team on Saturday afternoon revealed that Bills starting defensive tackle Ed Oliver is dealing with an oblique injury.

away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

home.headline: Bills' Week 12 injury report: DJ Moore not included, three starters added
home.blurb: As for tight end Dalton Kincaid, who missed the Week 11 win with a thumb, he was tabbed limited to start Week 12. When asked if Kincaid was close to being available this past Sunday, head coach Joe Brady said, "yeah." Benford did not practice in any official capacity last week en-route to being ruled out for Sunday's game on Friday. Brown was listed as a limited participant with Week 12 kicking off on Monday. Torrence, an unexpected addition to the injury report, also earned a limited designation. He's apparently dealing with an ankle issue coming out of Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Remaining on the injury report with the toe, Hamlin is also listed with a neck issue this week. He was officially limited on Monday. CB Christian Benford (groin) — DNP Bills' Updated Week 11 Injury Report: Christian Benford, Dalton Kincaid Remain Out The Buffalo Bills did not hold an official practice while kicking off their short week on Monday. Still, the Bills are required by the NFL to submit an injury report with estimated practice participations. Fulfilling that commitment, Buffalo listed 14 players who are dealing with injuries heading into the November 26 home game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. There are three notable additions to the Week 12 injury report. Technically, right tackle Spencer Brown, who endured a back flare-up in October, is a re-add due to the a reemergence of the issue. Meanwhile, starting right guard O'Cyrus Torrence has an ankle injury and Bills' sacks leader Greg Rousseau is listed due to a back problem. Rousseau made 2.0 sacks against Miami , and he was not showing signs of injury during postgame interactions. In a highly-encouraging development, wide receiver DJ Moore does not appear on the injury report . Moore hyperextended his leg late during the second quarter against the Miami Dolphins on November 22. He returned to action following a quick examination, finishing with nine receptions for 91 yards and one touchdown. "Sometimes, I wish he wasn't as tough, and it pains me to even say that," said head coach Joe Brady. "He's kind of like Josh, when he gets tackled, I just hope he gets up, because of how important he is." Starting outside cornerback Christian Benford, who was scratched from the lineup in Week 11, injured his groin during the second half against the New York Jets on November 15. As the Bills kicked off preparations for the Chiefs on Monday, Benford was the lone player listed as a non-participant. While the severity of his groin issue is not known publicly, it's presumed that the issue will sideline him for at least two weeks. Although we've been surprised before, with the Thanksgiving game being only 11 days after the injury occurred, it seems overly optimistic to expect Benford back in the lineup against the Chiefs. picks.blurb: Saints vs. Bears: Staff Picks and Score Predictions for Sunday Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2). Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. Prediction : Bears 32 Saints 21 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . Week 12 Waiver Wire 4 Bold Predictions for New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears in Week 11 Neal Coolong · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Soldier Field in late November isn't where a 3-6 team usually goes to turn its season around, but the New Orleans Saints are still one game behind Carolina in the NFC South. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. Two takeaways spring it, and the Saints leave Chicago at 4-6 with a 23-20 win. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
away.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears

home.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
home.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears

home.blurb: Hitting the road this Thanksgiving holiday? You might want to think twice about when you leave. New data has been released predicting the busiest travel times on roadways across the U.S. and some are far worse than others. According to AAA, an estimated 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30 this year. The good new is, that number is slightly lower than last year’s number, marking the end to a three-year trend that saw record highs. “After three years of record highs, the number of travelers is slightly lower partly because of higher travel costs this year. But travelers won’t notice much of a difference on the roads and at the airports, since projected volumes remain near record levels,” Stacey Barber, vice president of AAA Travel said in a statement. So when will the traffic be at its worst? “Drivers should consider hitting the road in the morning to avoid the heaviest congestion,” AAA suggested. For the Chicago area, AAA specifically cited the journey from Chicago to Indianapolis as one of the busiest routes, specifically via Interstate 65. That drive is expected to reach peak travel time around 4:30 p.m. on Nov. 30, when it is expected to see an 80% increase in travelers. The route is projected to take around five hours and 39 minutes. Typically, the drive would last an estimated three hours.

Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. away.blurb: Reports emerged on Saturday afternoon that an injured Tennessee Titans pass rusher was involved in a serious vehicle accident. Initial reports indicated that Jaylen Harrell was involved in the accident and was hospitalized with injuries. However, later reporting that Harrell’s level of involvement escalated into potential assault. Report: Titans Pass Rusher Involved In Severe Vehicle Incident Before Week 11 Showdown Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the allegations against the Titans pass rusher involved in the accident, so nothing substantive can be said yet. This is the third serious incident involving a Titans player in recent months. Calvin Ridley allegedly committed assault in Nashville, and Jordan Elliott was released after attempting to retrieve a firearm following an altercation with OT J.C. Latham. Ridley’s case is still being adjudicated, while Elliott landed another tryout opportunity with the Chicago Bears. The Titans released a boilerplate statement wishing Harrell and his family well after the accident, but revealed nothing before the seriousness of the allegations emerged. Now that the allegations are public, the league office and the franchise must do their due diligence. The Titans pass rusher has imperiled his career if these are ultimately proven true. This is the first known off-field incident that Harrell has been involved in since he entered the NFL as a seventh-round selection in the 2024 draft. Harrell landed on injured reserve during the 2026 preseason with an ACL injury, ending his season before it began. In two seasons, he has produced 38 tackles, seven tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks as a key reserve for the Titans. He was expected to contribute meaningful reps as a backup in 2026, but the injury made it impossible. The allegations are serious enough to warrant a further look by the franchise and league, as the Titans pass rusher involved himself to a degree that a second car was part of the incident. He allegedly assaulted the driver from the backseat, which caused the original vehicle to hit a second one and resulted in damage to a light pole in the end. As a result of the accident, Harrell was thrown forward against the windshield with enough force to require hospitalization. If he is found guilty of what is alleged, jail time is certainly on the table. Financially, the Titans would take a dead cap hit of $ 1,190,000 if he is released during the 2027 offseason, with cap savings of $20,184. It isn’t a huge number that could affect signings in the near future, but a mere rounding error on the cap sheet. As a former seventh-round selection still on his rookie contract, Harrell’s contract is a pittance to absorb easily. More than likely, he will get suspended and/or cut once the authorities, league, and the franchise complete the investigation. home.blurb: On Monday, the team hit the practice field at The Star for a walkthrough, which gave us an early look at who could be in danger of missing the game, with the first injury report of the week . Luckily, there was nothing out of the ordinary. Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle), star offensive lineman Tyler Booker (ankle), rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham (hip/groin), and linebacker Dee Winters (knee) were the four players who were held out of action. Winters was hurt during Sunday's win and was not expected to suit up, while the other three players have been out for the past week. For some positive news, we saw starting safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) return in limited fashion. Last week, the Dallas Cowboys' injury report was longer than a CVS receipt , so the first report for this week's game against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium is a positive sign. Dallas has a quick turnaround after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 , with just three days until returning to the field to face the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. Jalen Thompson (hamstring), one of the team's biggest free agent signings) also improved and was a full participant as he inches closer to returning to action for the first time since Week 3. home.headline: Tennessee Titans vs Dallas Cowboys: 6 things to know about Week 11
home.blurb: Both teams have struggled defensively, but the Cowboys' issues against the run could allow Tennessee to continue its recent positive offensive trajectory. Here are six intriguing storylines heading into Sunday's matchup at AT&T Stadium. 1. Both teams are coming off high-scoring losses High-scoring affairs have become a staple for the Cowboys this season, as they have played four games with a final score of both teams scoring 30 or more points. The highest of those games was their 46-40 loss to the 49ers last Sunday. Meanwhile, the Titans surrendered 40 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 40-23 loss, marking the second consecutive game in which Tennessee allowed at least 40 points. Their defense also gave up 43 points in its overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. Those results highlight a potential opportunity for a shootout on Sunday. For Tennessee, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down a Dallas offense that has demonstrated its ability to score against several opposing defenses all season long. 2. The Cowboys have the NFL's worst run defense One of the biggest advantages Tennessee could have entering Sunday's matchup is the Cowboys' struggles against the run. They rank last in the NFL in rushing defense, allowing 154.1 yards per game. That creates an appealing matchup for a Titans rushing attack that has shown signs of improvement in recent weeks against other weak run defenses. Tennessee rushed for 141 yards against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 (26th-ranked run defense) and followed that with 158 rushing yards against Cincinnati (21st-ranked run defense) in Week 8. The Titans also averaged a season-best 6.2 yards per carry collectively against Jacksonville in Week 10. Establishing the ground game early could help Tennessee control possession, keep Dallas' offense off the field, and create more manageable situations for quarterback Cam Ward. 3. Tony Pollard returns to Dallas for the first time since leaving Titans running back Tony Pollard spent the first five years of his career with the Cowboys, as was their full-time starter during his final season with them. Despite his success rushing for over 1000 yards in back-to-back seasons, the Titans prioritized Pollard more than Dallas during his free agency in 2024. Pollard has continued producing in Nashville, recording two additional 1000+ yard seasons and is on pace for his fifth straight year of achieving it with 628 rushing yards through nine games this season. With the Cowboys allowing the most rushing yards per game in the league, Pollard has an opportunity to make his former team pay for letting him leave. 4. The Cowboys won the last meeting between these teams in 2022 The Titans and Cowboys haven't met since December 29, 2022, when Dallas defeated Tennessee 27-13 on Thursday Night Football. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. Week 12 Waiver Wire 4 Bold Predictions for Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions in Week 11 Andrew Hughes · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:23 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come out of their bye at 3-6, and they've lost six games by seven points or fewer . A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. Tez Johnson catches a 40-yard pass Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson (15) makes a catch past Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Johnson has only 11 catches, but he's averaging 23.1 yards per reception with a long of 64, according to ESPN . Nobody else on the roster with more than five catches is close to that average. Detroit is playing without Aidan Hutchinson, and the Lions will have to respect Irving and the run game. One play-action shot to Johnson is the easiest way for a quarterback on a sore foot to change the game without having to move much. 3. The Bucs intercept Jared Goff twice Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish (25) intercepts a pass intended for Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) thrown by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (not pictured) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Goff has thrown four interceptions all season, so this one is bold. Tampa Bay has 21 takeaways , and 16 of them are interceptions. Zyon McCollum and Alex Anzalone have four apiece, and Jacob Parrish has two. Parrish draws Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he's PFF's No. 4 cornerback . If Goff keeps feeding St. Brown against Bowles' zone looks, the Bucs will get a couple of chances to jump a route. 4. Tampa Bay wins its first one-score game Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers placekicker Chase McLaughlin (4) celebrates with punter Riley Dixon (9) after kicking a thirty-four-yard field goal against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Bucs' three wins came by eight, 30 and 16 points. Every loss has been by seven or fewer, and the red zone is a big reason. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. away.headline: Which Buccaneers stepped up as injuries piled up before the bye?
away.blurb: His involvement was growing before the comparison period ended, reaching a season-high 30 defensive snaps against Carolina in Week 7. Walker's increased playing time is particularly important with Yaya Diaby dealing with a knee injury, although the available reporting does not establish that Walker's entire increase resulted from Diaby's absence. Injuries forced Tampa Bay to adjust before the bye, but the increased playing time also created opportunities to evaluate its depth. Chukwuma and Johnson showed they could contribute when starters were unavailable, while Durham, Sharp, and Walker earned bigger roles that could remain valuable in the second half of the season. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their Week 10 bye having dealt with injuries at quarterback, wide receiver, offensive tackle, and across the defense. Those absences forced lineup adjustments, but they also gave other players chances to show what they could contribute when called upon to step up. According to DepthRoom's snap-count data , five Buccaneers increased their share of playing time by at least 10 percentage points when comparing Weeks 4–6 with Weeks 7–9. Some stepped in for injured starters, while others saw their roles expand as personnel usage changed. Chukwuma saw the biggest increase, rising from 0% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in Weeks 4–6 to 33% over the next three games. His opportunity came when Luke Goedeke missed Week 7 against Carolina with a calf injury. Chukwuma started at right tackle and helped Tampa Bay rush for 258 yards in a 43-13 victory. According to Scott Smith's official team report , it was Chukwuma's third career start, and Todd Bowles expressed confidence in his potential to become a full-time NFL starter. Johnson's snap share climbed from 43% to 62%, with Emeka Egbuka's absence opening a spot at wide receiver. Egbuka missed Weeks 7 and 8 while dealing with concussion and foot injuries. Johnson started against Carolina and played 41 offensive snaps, contributing a 19-yard third-down reception, a 14-yard rushing gain, and a 14-yard touchdown catch. His involvement continued growing after Egbuka returned, reaching 54 snaps, or 79% of the offense, against Chicago in Week 9. Durham increased his offensive snap share from 26% to 46%, becoming a more frequent part of Tampa Bay's tight end rotation. The Buccaneers had already shown a willingness to use multiple tight ends, including opening their Week 6 matchup against Pittsburgh with three on the field. Durham's increase reflects a larger role in those personnel packages, although no specific injury has been established as the reason for his additional playing time. Perhaps the Egubka injury contributed to lineups with more tight ends on the field. Sharp's playing time rose from 6% to 23%, giving the rookie more opportunities alongside Cade Otton and Durham. home.headline: Detroit Lions Hit With Two Injury Concerns Before Thanksgiving Game
home.blurb: If he is limited or out, the Lions would lean more heavily on second-year edge rusher Ahmed Hassanein. Hassanein made his NFL debut Sunday and played 12 defensive snaps. Joseph played 46 snaps in his first action of the season. Christian Izien and Keith Abney remain available options if Clark is limited on Thursday. The estimated report also listed defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard (knee) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) as non-participants. Tight end Sam LaPorta was limited with an ankle injury. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Detroit Lions entered a short week with fresh injury concerns on defense ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown against the Chicago Bears. An estimated practice report released Monday listed edge rusher D.J. Wonnum as a non-participant with a back injury and safety Chuck Clark as a non-participant with a hamstring issue. The team held only a walkthrough, so the designations are estimates rather than results from a full session. Wonnum, one of the club’s key offseason additions, had not appeared on the injury report earlier in the week. He returned from a concussion that sidelined him for one game and contributed in Sunday’s 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The back issue raises questions about his availability for Thursday’s game at Ford Field. Head coach Dan Campbell was not asked about either player Monday and is expected to address the situation in his Tuesday news conference. Both absences would test a defense that has begun to stabilize after losing linebacker Jack Campbell and edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to longer-term injuries. Hutchinson remains on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury. Wonnum has recorded seven sacks in nine games this season, placing him one away from a career high. He played 49 defensive snaps (71 percent) against Tampa Bay, finishing with five tackles, a sack, a pass defensed and a forced fumble. Clark has started every game for Detroit this season and played every defensive snap against the Buccaneers, logging eight tackles, a sack and a pass defensed. The veteran was recently named a team captain after the losses of Campbell and Hutchinson. His absence could accelerate the integration of Kerby Joseph, who returned Sunday after a lengthy absence. The Lions used three-safety packages in that game, with Brian Branch shifting into the slot in nickel looks. Cornerbacks Khalil Dorsey (wrist) and D.J. Reed (hip) were listed as full participants, offering some stability in the secondary. Reed had been inactive for multiple recent games. Detroit (8-2) and Chicago (8-2) enter the game tied atop the NFC North. The Lions will have full practices Tuesday and Wednesday before submitting final injury designations. Campbell has emphasized the next-man-up approach throughout a season marked by absences. The estimated report provides the first public look at how the short week is affecting availability for the holiday matchup. This article

Will that trend continue in Week 11? Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game. The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona. Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win. Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him. Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches. Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks. With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game . Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense. With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense. The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense. Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Steve Spagnuolo's key will be limiting McBride, and with the Chiefs' cornerbacks holding down the outside, they should be able to do that. away.headline: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB's Status vs. Chiefs for NFL Week 11
away.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals will turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday. Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later. Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action. Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record. Even with Beck in the lineup, the 3-7 Cardinals were going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.

Until now, he had not been listed on the injury report since then. If Beck’s injury were to force him out of the game, the Cardinals would likely turn to veteran journeyman Josh Johnson, who served as their backup last week. Johnson was signed by the Cardinals on Nov. 10, along with Joey Aguilar, who was the third-string emergency quarterback last week. The Arizona Cardinals have added quarterback Carson Beck to the injury report, a potentially concerning development ahead of their Week 11 trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs. Start the day smarter. home.headline: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: What If Kenneth Walker Doesn't Play in Buffalo?
home.blurb: Should we be concerned if Ken Walker can't go in a HUGE game on Thursday? Would the groin injury knocking K9 out for at least three straight games affect your hopes for him going into January? - @EthanCo67716681 To fully wade into a hypothetical that might be irrelevant by the time Tuesday's injury report comes out: If Walker doesn't play in Buffalo, I think you have to have some level of concern about his timeline and expectations for the rest of the year, simply due to the possibility that a short-term injury, downplayed by the team, could be lingering much longer than the player and team expected. That's always alarming until the player returns and looks like their pre-injury self. There's also a possibility that we're overreacting to a Monday walkthrough "DNP" designation while Walker and the team could fully intend on having him suit up against the Bills. But in this moment of uncertainty, it's not what you'd want to see from the first estimated injury report of a short week. It's a short week, and the Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for the biggest game of their season so far, set to take on the Buffalo Bills in Orchard Park, New York, on Thanksgiving night. In this edition of the Chiefs On SI mailbag, all eyes are on Thursday night's AFC showdown, starting with a player who hasn't suited up for the Chiefs in the last two weeks. Well, it wouldn't be ideal! It certainly felt like the Chiefs were being cautious with Walker for the sake of getting him back to 100% for Thanksgiving night in Buffalo, but now we're left to monitor the injury reports with very little time for Walker to physically improve from however he felt before the Arizona Cardinals game. Add in the forecast of cold, wet, sloppy conditions expected on Thursday, and you have another element to be concerned about. That environment sounds like a recipe for a heavy workload for the game's running backs, but it's not ideal for a runner nursing a leg ailment. Meanwhile, to ask myself the next question: Is Walker still as important to the Chiefs' offense as he was a few weeks ago, before rookie running back Emmett Johnson put up back-to-back 100-yard rushing performances? I've been hugely impressed by Johnson's performances throughout the first half of his rookie season, and I think it's legitimate. No smoke and mirrors here; he's a quality NFL back. Still, Walker is obviously the more accomplished player, the more complete player, and he was an absolute revelation through the first act of the Chiefs' season. He also allows Johnson to become an overqualified No. 2 back when they're both healthy. home.headline: Cardinals find troubling injury report surprise ahead of Chiefs game
home.blurb: Beck was officially listed as limited for practice on Thursday, Nov. 19, with a back injury. He was later present in the locker room while it was open to reporters, and appeared to be walking around without discomfort. The injury report was first released shortly after the locker room closed to reporters. This is not the first time Beck has had back trouble this season, as he dealt with a back injury for two weeks in October. That injury first surfaced on Oct. 16. He missed two practices the following week and was listed as a limited participant three times, before returning to full participation on Oct. 29. Until now, he had not been listed on the injury report since then. If Beck’s injury were to force him out of the game, the Cardinals would likely turn to veteran journeyman Josh Johnson, who served as their backup last week. Johnson was signed by the Cardinals on Nov. 10, along with Joey Aguilar, who was the third-string emergency quarterback last week. The Arizona Cardinals have added quarterback Carson Beck to the injury report, a potentially concerning development ahead of their Week 11 trip to face the Kansas City Chiefs. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. “He’s just dealing with a bit of spasms,” head coach Mike LaFleur said on Oct. 23, of Beck’s previous injury. “It’s not like a long-term (issue) or anything like that. But trying to throw the way these guys throw, if you’re having a little bit of a back tweak, that’s what’s going on with him.” LaFleur’s next press conference is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, two days before the Cardinals’ game against the Chiefs in Kansas City. The bigger concern, though, would be the impact on Beck’s development, after an encouraging NFL debut in last week’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams. home.headline: Patrick Mahomes: Latest injury update, status report for Chiefs QB
home.blurb: Here is the latest update on Mahomes' status: Patrick Mahomes fully participated in the Chiefs' first practice session in Week 11 after injuring his elbow during Kansas City's victory over the New York Jets on November 8. He is also still nursing the knee injury that prematurely ended his 2025 campaign with the Chiefs. Will Patrick Mahomes play vs. Cardinals? For now, it seems Mahomes will be able to take the field against Arizona, but fans should monitor his status throughout the week to see if the two-time MVP suffers any setbacks during Kansas City's workouts. The Chiefs have veteran Justin Fields and rookie Garrett Nussmeier listed behind Mahomes on its depth chart. Fields would step in to replace Mahomes if the three-time Super Bowl champion is unable to play in Week 11.
