Week 12 Waiver Wire Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: According to NFL insider Benjamin Allbright, a league source indicated that the NFL may suspend Metcalf for his altercation with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean, in which he appeared to jam his fingers into DeJean's face. Different angles of the incident appear to show Metcalf attempting to poke DeJean in the eye, and the Steelers receiver was ultimately ejected from the game. We at Steelers Wire remain committed to providing any key details about Metcalf's potential suspension, with more information likely becoming available in the coming days. This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: NFL may suspend Steelers' DK Metcalf, per report Things may be getting ugly for Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf , as a new report indicates that the NFL may go the suspension route following his ejection from the Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles . Being ejected three times in his NFL career, Metcalf is also no stranger to suspensions, as he was handed a two-game punishment for his physical altercation with a Detroit Lions fan in 2025. If Metcalf is ultimately suspended for a game due to his immature antics against DeJean, the Steelers would be down to Roman Wilson, Germie Bernard, and potentially Michael Pittman Jr. as their top wide receivers in the Week 12 matchup against the Denver Broncos . home.headline: Dallas Cowboys' Injury Report Paints Promising Picture For Thanksgiving Game vs Eagles
home.blurb: On Monday, the team hit the practice field at The Star for a walkthrough, which gave us an early look at who could be in danger of missing the game, with the first injury report of the week . Luckily, there was nothing out of the ordinary. Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle), star offensive lineman Tyler Booker (ankle), rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham (hip/groin), and linebacker Dee Winters (knee) were the four players who were held out of action. Winters was hurt during Sunday's win and was not expected to suit up, while the other three players have been out for the past week. For some positive news, we saw starting safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) return in limited fashion. Last week, the Dallas Cowboys' injury report was longer than a CVS receipt , so the first report for this week's game against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium is a positive sign. Dallas has a quick turnaround after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 , with just three days until returning to the field to face the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. Jalen Thompson (hamstring), one of the team's biggest free agent signings) also improved and was a full participant as he inches closer to returning to action for the first time since Week 3. A full look at the first Cowboys injury report for Thanksgiving Week can be seen below. Derrick Henry is the focal point; Todd Wash and the defense will key in on him. Carolina has to win the time of possession battle here, Baltimore will crush the Panthers if they sustain long drives or get gifted first downs with penalties. The Panthers should be able to score here, not 30+ or anything, but enough to beat a mediocre Ravens offense. This game is going to be ugly like last week's was. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for this contest. At this point, it's difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven't had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn't moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No. X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he's been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations. Score Prediction: Panthers 31, Ravens 24 I'm not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn't fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter's defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn't seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can't stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win. X-Factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett's debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren't flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don't think the Jacoby-to-Ja'Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane's skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season. Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Ravens 17 The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens' recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina's offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina's struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher. Score Prediction: Ravens 27, Panthers 16 The Ravens' playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina's weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers' offensive tackles. X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young's biggest strength. Smith's coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let's see in this game. Score Prediction: Ravens 21, Panthers 20 It's hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday. X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike. Score Prediction: Panthers 26, Ravens 21

away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. away.blurb: While Jackson has not been officially ruled out for the season, he is expected to be sidelined for an extended period of time, and based on Baltimore's trajectory, it might be too late if and when he does actually return. While a Jackson trade seems incomprehensible, it might not be out of the realm of possibility. The 29-year-old has missed extensive time due to injuries the last two seasons. He sat out four games in 2025, and Baltimore ended up missing the playoffs. This year, he has played in just three contests. Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Report: Cubs, Japanese star Teruaki Satō agree to 6-year, $120M deal Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It certainly has not been an easy year for Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Jackson missed three games early on in the 2026 NFL campaign due to an ankle injury. Then, after returning in Week 8, he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive snap, which ultimately resulted in surgery. Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork provided an update on Jackson's status Thursday, and unfortunately, he didn't seem to have anything substantial to add. "He's been in and he's focused on his rehab right now," Woolfork told The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec . What is Lamar Jackson's future with the Baltimore Ravens? The two-time MVP is nearing the climax of a five-year, $260 million deal with the club, one that ends after 2027. There has been speculation that the Ravens could potentially look to trade Jackson before extending him. Given the clear wear-and-tear on Jackson's body, it is fair to wonder if parting ways would be the best thing for both sides this offseason. The Ravens' window seems to be closing, and with Jackson's health deteriorating, Baltimore might be better off starting from scratch. Whether or not it actually happens, of course, remains to be seen. home.headline: Panthers give injury update on WR Jalen Coker heading into Week 12
home.blurb: Carolina Panthers wideout Jalen Coker is all clear. The third-year receiver exited yesterday's 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens late in the fourth quarter. Coker took a big hit over the middle from linebacker Roquan Smith on a 6-yard reception, and was sent into concussion protocol. The New York Jets could turn to rookie Cade Klubnik for his first NFL start Sunday, with Geno Smith’s ankle injury leaving coach Aaron Glenn without a firm answer at quarterback. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Glenn said. The decision concerns Smith’s health, not an announced benching. Glenn said Monday that Smith would retain the job if healthy, The Associated Press reported . Tests did not reveal a serious ankle injury, but New York still needs to determine whether he can play. The Jets are 2-8 after five consecutive losses. They have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, and a change at quarterback would put a fourth-round pick from Clemson in charge of an offense struggling to finish drives. Klubnik made his professional debut against Buffalo and completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards with an interception. He also ran three times for 26 yards. Glenn praised the rookie’s mobility Wednesday and said he would continue getting practice opportunities against the first- and second-team defenses. Klubnik had little time to settle in, but his first possession produced a 10-play, 61-yard drive and a field goal. Two scrambles moved the chains on that series, the team reported Monday . He played 37 snaps in relief of Smith. Running back Breece Hall came away encouraged by how Klubnik handled the huddle. Hall said the rookie showed more than he expected while stepping into a game without the preparation afforded a starter. “Just seeing how he came in, that was a huge growth step for him,” Hall said. I’ve known Joe for a long time. Ironically, he was actually at Texas with my son a few years ago. So I think it starts with coaching. When you watch them on film, a huge emphasis in the phases. away.blurb: Injury Report: S Talanoa Hufanga among Broncos not assigned game statuses, S Brandon Jones questionable for Week 11 vs. Raiders Skip to main content Primary nav Game Day ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — Multiple Broncos appear poised to make their return to game action in Week 11 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (concussion) and cornerback Riley Moss (concussion) were among Denver's players who were not assigned game statuses on the Broncos' final practice report of the week, which indicates they will be available to play. All three players were full participants throughout the week. Waddle and Moss, who suffered their respective injuries against the Panthers in Week 9, will also be set to return to the field. Moss signed a four-year contract extension on Thursday. Safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) was the lone Broncos player listed as questionable. Jones, who exited Denver's Week 8 win over Kansas City with his injury, was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11. Tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) was a full participant in all three practices as he returned to practice this week, but he was ruled out for Sunday's game. Jones, who was listed as questionable after he was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11, was among the team's inactive players. Hufanga appears set to play for the first time since suffering his injury in Week 5 against the Chargers. They are the only team in the division with a positive point differential (+7). They are also pretty angry about having blown a chance against the Washington Commanders last week, a loss that gives the third-place Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker if the two teams somehow end up with the same win-loss record at the end of the season. All of these factors have some critics snickering about the Giants' current standing. After all, someone has to be in first place, regardless of the division, right? And it's not that the Giants care what those outside of 1925 Giants Drive think about their team. Still, they can certainly make a statement with a convincing upset win over the Jaguars, who, surprisingly, FanDuel Sportsbook lists as only a 5.5-point favorite over Big Blue. Will the Giants come through and get their first home win since a 36-24 triumph over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 4, 2026? Let's dive in. Why the Giants Will Win The easiest way for the Giants to win this game is to keep the Jaguars offense off the field. And it just so happens that the Giants are currently second in the league in average time of possession (32:26), behind the league-leading Chicago Bears (34:31). That's not bad considering the Giants' rushing game ranks 18th in the league (112.6 yards per game). Big Blue averages 5.7 plays per drive, tying it for seventh in the league (Jacksonville averages 5.8 plays per drive, for those wondering). Defensively, the Giants have been strong against the deep ball, which just so happens to be Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence's superpower. Lawrence has a 51.6 percent completion rate on passes of 20-plus air yards this season, fifth in the league. The Giants have a 38.4 percent blitz rate this season, fourth in the league, and have blitzed on 50 percent or more of their plays since Week 4, a 20 percent increase from the first three weeks. In terms of coverage, the Giants lead the league with a 17.2 percent completion rate allowed on deep balls of 20-plus air yards. They are also the only team not to allow a touchdown on a deep pass attempt, and they have four interceptions on those passes, tied for second in the league. Why the Giants Won't Beat the Jaguars Two potential reasons could doom the Giants' chances of scoring their first home win in over a month. The first is turnovers. The opportunistic Jaguars lead the league with a +9 turnover differential, having 16 takeaways to only seven giveaways. The Jaguars' takeaways include 12 interceptions ( fourth in the league ). The Giants currently have a -2 turnover differential, 21st in the league. They have three giveaways in their last three games (one interception and two lost fumbles). Fumbling has been an issue for the Giants, who have had six fumbles in their last two games. That's not good against an opportunistic Jacksonville team that is averaging 2.3 takeaways over its last three games. Give the Jaguars a short field to work with, and that's asking for trouble. The other thing to watch is the Jaguars' first-half scoring. The Jaguars lead the league in first-half scoring, averaging 15.89 points within the first 30 minutes of regulation. The Giants, meanwhile, have averaged 9.44 points per game in the first half. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. Week 12 Waiver Wire NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

away.blurb: Former third-round pick Wyatt Milum came in at left tackle with Little out. He was not healthy in the offseason and did not have much free-agent attention. With all of the starting spots filled, he has been waiting for the right fit and situation to return. The Jaguars would present that. Jaguars Urged to Sign Pro Bowler Amid Injuries Unlock the latest Heavy on Jaguars news — direct to your inbox. The Jacksonville Jaguars could be down to their third left tackle when they face the Tennessee Titans in Week 12. One potential move they could make to ensure the offensive line still has talent heading into their playoff push is signing free agent left tackle Taylor Decker, according to Moe Moton of Bleacher Report . Moton noted that the combination of the Jaguars' loss in Week 11 along with the experience of Decker makes for a good fit. “Last Sunday, the Giants consistently pressured Lawrence, who took three sacks in a loss,” wrote Moton. “Other teams will look at that game and likely try to emulate what Big Blue did to rattle Lawrence in the pocket, and it would be easier to do that against a third-string left tackle. Taylor Decker is a 10-year starter who would fit the Jaguars' need at left tackle if the team must choose another fill-in replacement. Last year, with the Detroit Lions, he allowed just two sacks over 551 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus.” Jacksonville Jaguars Could Sign Taylor Decker Anton Harrison is not coming back this season. Head coach Liam Coen implied that the Little injury will not be serious, but there is a chance that he will miss Week 12. Milum played tackle in college, but they drafted him with the plan to have him play guard in the NFL. This is where he spent most of his time in the preseason and practice. So, he could start if needed, but it would not be a strong option. Adding Decker would give them a starter in the short term and depth that appears to be needed for a playoff run. Decker is a Fit for Jaguars Playoff Push The former first-round pick from Ohio State is a ten-year veteran in the NFL. Decker has made 140 career starts and made the Pro Bowl in 2024. However, he was not as good in 2025 and finished the season with a couple of injuries. Decker could earn starting work for the Jags, which could help him prolong his career into the 2027 season. He could also help a contender make a playoff push. Decker has only played in five playoff games. So, getting a chance to make a run would be enticing. The Jaguars could use the veteran pressence and Decker could use them to help his resume. It makes sense on both sides. We will see how confident the Jags are in Little based on his practice status this week. away.headline: Tee Higgins touchdown sparks 'rigged' NFL claims after Jaguars catch ruled out
away.blurb: • Bengals fans hit out at NFL referees for missing late hit on Joe Burrow Higgins' touchdown shortly before halftime provided the Bengals a 10-0 advantage before Jacory Croskey-Merritt scored from a yard out for Washington. The Bengals headed into the second half up 10-7, with Higgins tallying 31 receiving yards. Tee Higgins produced a spectacular catch in wet conditions that could feature on ESPN's Sportscenter Top 10 any week, but the strongest reaction came from Jacksonville Jaguars supporters who witnessed a nearly identical play ruled incomplete less than 24 hours prior. Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow connected with Higgins for a 31-yard touchdown during Monday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, with the receiver making a diving over-the-shoulder grab in the end zone. Officials credited Higgins and the Bengals with the touchdown despite minor movement of the ball as Higgins completed the play on the wet and rain-soaked turf of Northwest Stadium, fueling fresh claims that the NFL is rigged. • Jayden Daniels leads game-winning drive as Commanders beat Bengals on MNF This prompted viewers to recall Sunday's Jaguars matchup against the New York Giants , where Parker Washington had a comparable touchdown attempt ruled incomplete. Jacksonville appealed the call, but the decision was upheld, leaving Jaguars supporters outraged. Washington stated postgame that he felt he made the catch but quickly accepted the outcome, acknowledging the nature of NFL officiating, reports the Mirror US . ESPN play-by-play commentator Joe Buck drew the parallel between the two receptions immediately following Higgins' score. Buck and Aikman encountered visible hostility from fans and a power failure that briefly left them in darkness. Buck questioned why the Bengals receiver was awarded six points when Washington's apparent touchdown against New York was disallowed less than 24 hours earlier. Rules analyst Russell Yurk stated both plays should have been ruled touchdowns and that the real problem was how Sunday's play was assessed. On Higgins' touchdown, the receiver seemed to control the ball with both hands while getting a foot down beyond the goal line. His knees touched down in the end zone before the football moved, its tip grazing the turf as he fell. The controversial sequence had NFL fans drawing comparisons between both moments online. "NFL just changing what a catch is overnight," one fan posted. Some frustrated spectators accused the NFL of "rigged" games. • Antonio Williams avoids serious injury but NFL fans unhappy with referees • GTA VI fans told to 'read a book' rather than play new game by Chris Russo League vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth stated officials didn't observe sufficient control to reverse the original incomplete-pass call on Washington's catch. away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo celebrated his team's 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars by doing something he said he said he wouldn't do again: a backflip. home.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
home.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. away.headline: NFL-49ers rout Vikings as NFL makes electrifying return to Mexico
away.blurb: MEXICO CITY, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The San Francisco 49ers overwhelmed the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 on Sunday at the Azteca Stadium, as the National Football League made a thrilling return to Mexico City after a four-year absence with its first international Sunday Night Football game. The halftime show featured Mexican rock trio The Warning, as the break was extended by six minutes to accommodate the teams' return from locker rooms located outside the stadium. By Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina More than 85,000 fans, most of them backing the 49ers, filled the stadium, underlining the popularity of the sport in Mexico, which is the NFL's largest market outside the US. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell had described the occasion as a "mini-Super Bowl", underlining the importance of a country that has hosted five previous regular-season games since the league first played in Mexico in 2005. San Francisco quickly gave its supporters something to cheer when tight end George Kittle opened the scoring on the 49ers' first possession. Kittle, one of the most popular players among Mexican fans, added another touchdown in the second quarter, his fourth in the Mexican capital. Minnesota responded with an 11-yard touchdown run by Aaron Jones but struggled to cope with San Francisco's offense and the deafening noise inside the stadium. The 49ers extended their lead through a touchdown pass from quarterback Brock Purdy to Mike Evans before safety Ji'Ayir Brown intercepted Kirk Cousins and returned the ball 18 yards for a touchdown to make it 28-10 at halftime. The 49ers' right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field on a stretcher after suffering a lower-leg injury in the second quarter, prompting an emotional reaction from teammates. Purdy cemented his status as an MVP contender with a dominant performance against a Minnesota defense that had entered the game allowing an NFL-best 14 points per contest. He threw three touchdown passes in the first half alone. San Francisco maintained control after the interval, with cornerback Deommodore Lenoir forcing a fumble from Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson in the third quarter. Running back Christian McCaffrey added a 6-yard touchdown early in the final quarter to stretch the lead as visibly fatigued players used oxygen masks on the sidelines to cope with the effects of playing at an altitude of more than 2,200 meters (7,217 ft) above sea level. Some Minnesota supporters began leaving the stands as their team struggled to mount a comeback. San Francisco had made special preparations for the altitude, spending the week training at the US Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while Minnesota remained at home and used a specially constructed altitude-training room at its facility. The matchup was the final stop on the NFL's record nine-game international schedule this season. (Reporting by Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina in Mexico City)

He threw three touchdown passes in the first half alone. San Francisco maintained control after the interval, with cornerback Deommodore Lenoir forcing a fumble from Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson in the third quarter. Running back Christian McCaffrey added a 6-yard touchdown early in the final quarter to stretch the lead as visibly fatigued players used oxygen masks on the sidelines to cope with the effects of playing at an altitude of more than 2,200 meters (7,217 ft) above sea level. Some Minnesota supporters began leaving the stands as their team struggled to mount a comeback. San Francisco had made special preparations for the altitude, spending the week training at the US Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while Minnesota remained at home and used a specially constructed altitude-training room at its facility. The matchup was the final stop on the NFL's record nine-game international schedule this season. (Reporting by Janina Nuno Rios and Angelica Medina in Mexico City)

home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray are out as expected, while just Jay Ward and Isaiah Rodgers are listed as questionable. Kevin O’Connell said that Rodgers felt good in Friday’s practice but was limited, and they will see how he feels after practice and with post-practice treatment. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Monday night contest in DC Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals . Washington enters this game having won two of its last three since returning from the bye. The Commanders scored a come-from-behind victory over the division rival New York Giants last week, keeping their hopes alive in the NFC East in the process. Jayden Daniels and Co. are still just 3-5-1 on the season, but given the relative weaknesses of the NFC East, they can count themselves as divisional contenders if they can string together some wins over the next few weeks. Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are red hot, having won five in a row while scoring at least 31 points in each of those contests. Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are tearing holes in opposing defenses, and Cincinnati's own defense is much improved since last year. The Bengals can open up a two-game lead in the division with a win on Monday night. Will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling? We'll find out soon enough as kickoff is approaching. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Commanders vs. Bengals live Date: Monday, Nov. 23 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Northwest Stadium (Landover, Maryland) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -6, O/U 54.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bengals have the ball Joe Burrow enters this game as the MVP favorite and the hottest quarterback in the NFL . Burrow is leading the NFL in completions, completion percentage, touchdowns, first downs, yards per game, success rate, passer rating and QBR while ranking second in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Over the last five games, he is practically touching the surface of the sun, completing 77.6% of his passes at an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdown passes and three interceptions. He's totaled at least four scores in each of those five games, tying a league-record streak. During that stretch, his 0.42 EPA per dropback mark is more than 50% better than the second-place player, Trevor Lawrence (0.26), per Tru Media. He is shredding every single coverage with ease. Ja'Marr Chase is on nearly as much of a heater as is Burrow. Chase has a 43-666-4 receiving line since the Bengals' Week 5, and he's recorded at least 10 catches for 141 yards in each of the Bengals' last three games. Last week, he went off for 231 yards against the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers — the fourth 200-plus-yard game of his career. The Commanders, needless to say, do not have anybody who has a hope of guarding him. The Commies have been known to double opposing No. 1 wideouts more often than other teams this season, but even doing that might not necessarily be wise because Tee Higgins is playing the best football of his career as well. Higgins has a 53-824-6 receiving line so far this season, as he's averaging a career-best 91.6 receiving yards per game. He's been a bit quieter than Chase over the last two weeks, but he still has 10 grabs for 88 yards and two touchdowns in that time. His size and physicality make him a nightmare matchup for any cornerback, especially with Burrow playing as well as he is at the moment. Meanwhile, the Commanders have allowed the NFL's fourth-most completions to tight ends so far this season, as well as the second-most yards and touchdowns. That could open up opportunities for Mike Gesicki and/or Drew Sample , though Gesicki is obviously the bigger receiving threat of the two. Washington has actually been somewhat solid against the run this season, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. Opposing offensive lines have cleared the way for only 1.08 yards before contact per rush, according to Tru Media, and the second-level defenders have limited rushers to the third-lowest broken tackle rate in the league. However, the Bengals basically only run the ball as an occasional changeup, with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine acting as receivers nearly as often as they do runners. Even if the Commanders shut down the run game, it seems unlikely to matter much to Cincinnati's offensive success. Everything runs through Burrow, Chase and Higgins. When the Commanders have the ball Jayden Daniels has been efficient since his return from his elbow injury, completing 67.3% of his passes at an average of 7.6 yards per attempt. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions, along with 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries across five games during which the Commanders have compiled a 2-2-1 record. Daniels hasn't been particularly explosive during that stretch, but he has kept the chains moving for the most part, and the Commies have been able to stay in games against the Giants (twice) and Eagles while losing by only one score to the 49ers and Rams . Without Terry McLaurin , Daniels' top targets are Stefon Diggs , rookie Antonio Williams , Treylon Burks , Van Jefferson and tight end Chig Okonkwo. Diggs is mostly a short-area target who splits his time between the perimeter and the slot. He works the underneath zones as Daniels tries to matriculate the ball down the field. Williams has become a bigger part of the rotation in recent weeks but hasn't really popped off that much despite the increase in role. Burks is a rotational deep threat who has seen his snap share increase since McLaurin went down, while Jefferson works in behind each of the top three. Okonkwo is a short-area chain mover similar to Diggs, but with perhaps more run-after-catch ability relative to his position. The Bengals are surprisingly 12th in the NFL in net yards allowed per attempt (which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks), and they have allowed only 11 passing touchdowns so far this season. They have a solid enough group of defensive backs, including one star in DJ Turner II, and their tackling has improved significantly on the second level of the defense this year. The Commanders don't have much of a run game to speak of, what with their stable of backs combining to average just 3.7 yards per carry this season. They'll get Jacory Croskey-Merritt back on Monday night, but even he is only at 3.6 yards per carry this season. He's likely to split work with both Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler , each of whom is better in the passing game than they are when running the football. With big Dexter Lawrence in the middle of the defensive line, it could be difficult for Washington to get anything going on the ground, even though the Bengals have actually been hit for 5.0 yards per opponent rush attempt so far this season. Lawrence has near single-handedly taken over a few games or stretches of possessions, even if teams like the Dolphins , Titans and Falcons have been able to find holes on the ground. The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even in winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. away.blurb: India, Nov. 24 -- The Washington Commanders will be without cornerback Amik Robertson for their Week 11 Monday Night Football clash against the Cincinnati Bengals, as the defensive back has been ruled inactive due to an ankle injury. Robertson picked up the problem during the final play of Friday's practice and was subsequently unable to participate in Saturday's session. Although he was initially listed as questionable, the 28-year-old's absence was confirmed after he struggled to test the injury during pregame warmups. "It was sore today, so we held (him) out," Quinn said on November 21, adding that the team would monitor his condition over the following 48 hours. Center Lucas Patrick (concussion), cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle) and running backs Rachaad White (heel) and Bill Croskey-Merritt (groin) are the questionable players, though not all questionable designations are equal in this instance. Croskey-Merritt was also listed as questionable to play against the Bengals, though that designation is standard among players on injured reserve in their practice windows . The verdict on Croskey-Merritt’s status will come on Monday, when he’s activated (or not). After a week of full participation, it’s fair to expect Croskey-Merritt to be available. While receiver Treylon Burks was a DNP on Friday, it was an injury management play as he works to get his foot issue right. He didn’t receive a designation and will be available to play. Despite being limited during the practice week, safety Quan Martin (shoulder) will be available to play the Bengals. Who’s in, who’s out for Monday’s game between the Commanders and Bengals? He was also optimistic about White, stating that the veteran RB skipped Saturday’s work to quiet some soreness in his heel. While Quinn wasn’t completely direct regarding White, it sure seems like he’s going to play. Robertson, however, is truly up in the air. He suffered an ankle injury on the last play of Friday’s practice and didn’t participate on Saturday. The Commanders will see how the ailment responds between now and game time before making a call on Robertson. If he can’t go, Rasul Douglas would play a lot more, with Mike Sainristil and Fabian Moreau helping some in the slot.
